title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
abstract: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.

informal.SumDifferenceExponent.growthExponent_lt_: For every finite set A of integers with at least two elements, log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.tendsto_growthExpo: The growth exponents of the explicit finite integer sets approximatingSet l converge to 2 as l tends to infinity; these sets have at least two elements whenever l is positive.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.isLUB_admissibleEx: The number 2 is the least upper bound of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.sSup_admissibleExp: The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.supremum_not_attai: No finite integer set with at least two elements has growth exponent equal to 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.quantitative_examp: The explicitly defined finite integer set quantitativeSet has growth exponent strictly between 2 - 10^(-999) and 2.
